title: Rock from deep underground
text: In the Tehachapi Mountains, rock that formed 25 to 30 kilometers below the surface now lies exposed. These are Cretaceous gneisses from deep within the Sierra Nevada batholith. Seismic profiles show that the batholith rocks dip northward as a tilted slab beneath the southern end of the San Joaquin Basin.

s1.title: Significance of seismic reflections beneath a tilted exposure of deep continental crust, Tehachapi Mountains, California
s1.quote: Cretaceous gneisses that formed 25-30 km down in the Sierra Nevada batholith ... batholithic rocks dip northward as a tilted slab and extend beneath the southern end of the San Joaquin Basin's Tejon embayment
